descriptionChirho: A masculine noun denoting something desirable, delightful, or precious — used attributively to describe objects of aesthetic or emotional value. Appears in contexts of desirable/pleasant things: 'vessels of desire/delight' (2 Chr 36:19; Dan 11:8), 'land of delight' (Mal 3:12; Zech 7:14), and 'all precious/pleasant stones' (Isa 54:12). The multilingual evidence shows a unified semantic field: eng: desire/delight, spa: deseo/deleite/delicia, arb: مُشْتَهُونَ / بَهِيٌّ / بَهجَةٍ (all in the semantic range of beauty/desirability), kor: 아름다운/기쁜 (beautiful/joyful), hin: मनभावन/मनोहर/सुंदर (attractive/beautiful), swa: kupendeza/zuri (pleasing/fine). The three clusters are not semantically distinct — 'desire', 'delight', and 'delight' overlap entirely as facets of the same quality of preciousness or desirability.
